body.text: oṃ pañcātmakaṃ pañcasu vartamānaṃ ṣaḍāśrayaṃ ṣaḍguṇayogayuktam / taṃ saptadhātuṃ trimalaṃ dviyoniṃ caturvidhāhāramayaṃ śarīram || GarUp_1
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. The body is composed of five elements, existing within the five, having six supports, endowed with the conjunction of six qualities, comprising seven <s>dhātus</s> (tissues), three impurities, two origins, and is made of four kinds of food.

body.text: pañcātmakam iti kasmāt pṛthivy āpas tejo vāyur ākāśam ity asmin pañcātmake śarīre kā pṛthivī kā āpaḥ kiṃ tejaḥ ko vāyuḥ kim ākāśam / tatra pañcātmake śarīre yat kaṭhinaṃ sā pṛthivī yad dravaṃ tā āpaḥ yad uṣṇaṃ tat tejaḥ yat saṃcarati sa vāyuḥ yac chuṣiraṃ tad ākāśam / tatra pṛthivī dhāraṇe āpaḥ piṇḍīkaraṇe tejaḥ prakāśane vāyur vyūhane ākāśam avakāśapradāne / pṛthak śrotre śabdopalabdhau tvak sparśe cakṣuṣī rūpe jihvā rasane nāsikā ghrāṇe upastha ānandane apānam utsarge buddhyā budhyati manasā saṃkalpayati vācā vadati / ṣaḍāśrayam iti kasmāt madhurāmlalavaṇatiktakaṭukaṣāyarasān vindatīti ṣaḍjaṛṣabhagāndhāramadhyamapañcamadhaivataniṣādāś cetīṣṭāniṣṭaśabdasaṃjñāḥ praṇidhānād daśavidhā bhavanti || GarUp_2
body.translated_text: 'Composed of five elements' — why? Because earth, water, fire, air, and space are in this body composed of five elements. What is earth? What is water? What is fire? What is air? What is space? In this body of five elements, that which is hard is earth; that which is liquid is water; that which is hot is fire; that which moves is air; that which is hollow is space. Of these, earth serves in supporting, water in cohesion, fire in illumination, air in distribution, and space in providing room. Separately, the ear in perceiving sound, the skin in touch, the eyes in form, the tongue in taste, the nose in smell, the generative organ in pleasure, the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) in excretion; one cognizes with the intellect, resolves with the mind, and speaks with speech. 'Having six supports' — why? Because it experiences sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent tastes. <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, and <s>niṣāda</s> — these are the designations of pleasant and unpleasant sounds; through attentive perception they become tenfold.

body.text: saptadhātukam iti kasmāt śuklo raktaḥ kṛṣṇo dhūmraḥ pītaḥ kapilaḥ pāṇḍura iti / yathā devadattasya dravyādiviṣayā jāyante / parasparaṃ saumyaguṇatvāt ṣaḍvidho rasaḥ rasāc choṇitaṃ śoṇitān māṃsaṃ māṃsān medo medasaḥ snāyavaḥ snāyubhyo 'sthīni asthibhyo majjā majjātaḥ śukraṃ śukraśoṇitasaṃyogād āvartate garbho hṛdi vyavasthāṃ nayati hṛdaye 'ntar āgniḥ agnisthāne pittaṃ pittasthāne vāyuḥ vāyuto hṛdayaṃ prājāpatyāt kramāt || GarUp_3
body.translated_text: 'Comprising seven <s>dhātus</s> (tissues)' — why? White, red, black, smoky, yellow, tawny, and pale — just as the objects and other things of <s>Devadatta</s> come into being. Because of the mutual quality of being gentle, taste is sixfold: from <s>rasa</s> (chyle) comes blood; from blood, flesh; from flesh, fat; from fat, sinews; from sinews, bones; from bones, marrow; from marrow, semen. From the union of semen and blood, the embryo forms and becomes established in the heart. Within the heart is the inner fire; in the place of fire is bile; in the place of bile is air; from air the heart functions, in the order established by <s>Prajāpati</s>.

body.text: ṛtukāle samprayogād ekarātroṣitaṃ kalalaṃ bhavati saptarātroṣitaṃ budbudam ardhamāsābhyantare piṇḍaṃ māsābhyantare kaṭhinaṃ māsadvayena śiraḥ māsatrayeṇa pādapradeśaḥ caturthe gulphajaṭharakaṭipradeśāḥ pañcame pṛṣṭhavaṃśaḥ ṣaṣṭhe mukhanāsikākṣiśrotrāṇi saptame jīvena saṃyuktaḥ aṣṭame sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇaḥ / pitū reto'tirekāt puruṣaḥ mātū reto'tirekāt strī ubhayor vojatulyatvān napaṃusakaṃ vyākulitamanaso 'ndhāḥ khañcāḥ kubjā vāmanā bhavanti / anyo 'nyavāyuparipīḍitaśukradvaidhyād dvidhā tanū syād yugmāḥ prajāyante / pañcātmakaḥ samarthaḥ pañcātmikā cetasā buddhir gandharasādijñānākṣarākṣaram oṃkāraṃ cintayatīti tad ekākṣaraṃ jñātvāṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ ṣoḍaśa vikārāḥ śarīre tasyaiva dehinaḥ / atha mātrāśitapītanāḍīsūtragatena prāṇa āpyāyate / atha navame māsi sarvalakṣaṇajñānasampūrṇo bhavati pūrvajātiṃ smarati śubhāśubhaṃ ca karma vindati || GarUp_4
body.translated_text: From union at the proper season, after one night's stay it becomes <s>kalala</s> (a gelatinous mass); after seven nights, a bubble; within a fortnight, a solid lump; within a month, it hardens; in two months, the head forms; in three months, the region of the feet; in the fourth month, the ankle, belly, and hip regions; in the fifth, the spinal column; in the sixth, the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears; in the seventh, it becomes joined with the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); in the eighth, it is complete with all features. If the father's seed predominates, it becomes male; if the mother's seed predominates, female; if the vigor of both is equal, a eunuch. If the minds of the parents are disturbed, the offspring will be blind, lame, hunchbacked, or dwarfed. If the semen is split in two by the mutual pressure of the winds, twins are born. The body of five elements becomes capable; the mind of five elements, through intellect, knows smell, taste, and other perceptions, and contemplates the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, both perishable and imperishable. Having known that one syllable, there are eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (primal substances) and sixteen <s>vikāras</s> (modifications) in the body of that very embodied being. Then, through the channels of the mother's food and drink, <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is nourished. Then in the ninth month, the embryo becomes complete with all features and knowledge, remembers its former births, and perceives both good and bad <s>karma</s> (actions).

children.translated_text: Having seen thousands of previous wombs,

children.text: āhārā vividhā bhuktāḥ pītā nānāvidhāḥ stanāḥ /
children.translated_text: various foods were eaten and diverse breasts were suckled by me;

children.text: jātaś caiva mṛtaś caiva janma caiva punaḥ punaḥ || GarUp_5
children.translated_text: having been born and having died, there is birth again and again.

children.text: yan mayā parijanasyārthe kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham /
children.translated_text: Whatever good and bad <s>karma</s> (action) was performed by me for the sake of others,

children.text: ekākī tena dahye 'haṃ gatās te phalabhoginaḥ || GarUp_6
children.translated_text: alone I am burned by it; those who enjoyed the fruits have departed.

children.text: aho duḥkhodadhau magno na paśyāmi pratikriyām /
children.translated_text: Alas! Plunged in the ocean of sorrow, I see no remedy.

children.text: yadi yonyāḥ pramucye 'haṃ tat prapadye maheśvaram || GarUp_7
children.translated_text: If I am released from the womb, I shall take refuge in <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord),
the destroyer of inauspicious <s>karma</s> and the bestower of the fruit of liberation.

children.text: yadi yonyāḥ pramucye 'haṃ tat prapadye nārāyaṇam || GarUp_8
children.translated_text: If I am released from the womb, I shall take refuge in <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
the destroyer of inauspicious <s>karma</s> and the bestower of the fruit of liberation.

children.text: yadi yonyāḥ pramucye 'haṃ tat sāṃkhyaṃ yogam abhyase || GarUp_9
children.translated_text: If I am released from the womb, I shall practice <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>,
which destroy inauspicious <s>karma</s> and bestow the fruit of liberation.

children.text: yadi yonyāḥ pramuñcāmi dhyāye brahma sanātanam || GarUp_10
children.translated_text: If I am released from the womb, I shall meditate upon eternal <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: atha yonidvāraṃ samprāpto yantreṇāpīḍyamāno mahatā duḥkhena jātamātras tu vaiṣṇavena vāyunā saṃspṛṣṭas tadā na smarati janma maraṇāni na ca karma śubhāśubhaṃ vindati || GarUp_11
body.translated_text: Then, having reached the opening of the womb, being pressed by the mechanism of birth, with great suffering — as soon as born, being touched by the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> wind (the external air), one no longer remembers birth and death, nor perceives good and bad <s>karma</s>.

body.text: śarīram iti kasmāt agnayo hy atra śriyante jñānāgnir darśanāgniḥ koṣṭhāgnir iti tatra koṣṭhāgnir nāmāśitapītalehyacoṣyaṃ pacati / darśanāgnī rūpāṇāṃ darśanaṃ karoti / jñānāgniḥ śubhāśubhaṃ ca karma vindati / trīṇi sthānāni bhavanti mukhe āhavanīya udare gārhapatyo hṛdi dakṣiṇāgniḥ ātmā yajamāno mano brahmā lobhādayaḥ paśavo dhṛtir dīkṣā saṃtoṣaś ca buddhīndriyāṇi yajñapātrāṇi karmendriyāṇi havīṃṣi śiraḥ kapālaṃ keśā darbhāḥ mukham antarvediḥ catuṣkapālaṃ śiraḥ ṣoḍaśa pārśvadantapaṭalāni saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ sāśītikaṃ saṃdhiśataṃ sanavakaṃ snāyuśataṃ sapta sirāśatāni pañca majjāśatāni asthīni ca ha vai trīṇi śatāni ṣaṣṭiḥ sārdhacatasro romāṇi koṭyo hṛdayaṃ palāny aṣṭau dvādaśa palā jihvā pittaprasthaṃ kaphasyāḍhakaṃ śukrakuḍavaṃ medaḥ prasthau dvāv aniyataṃ mūtrapurīṣam āhāraparimāṇāt / paippalādaṃ mokṣaśāstraṃ paippalādaṃ mokṣaśāstram iti || GarUp_12
body.translated_text: Why is it called <s>śarīra</s> (body)? Because fires (<s>agni</s>) are sheltered (<s>śriyante</s>) herein — the fire of knowledge (<s>jñānāgni</s>), the fire of sight (<s>darśanāgni</s>), and the fire of the belly (<s>koṣṭhāgni</s>). Of these, the fire of the belly digests what is eaten, drunk, licked, and sucked. The fire of sight causes the perception of forms. The fire of knowledge discerns good and bad <s>karma</s> (action). There are three stations of fire: in the mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (the offering fire), in the belly is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (the household fire), in the heart is the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (the southern fire). The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>); the mind is the officiating priest (<s>Brahmā</s>); greed and the other passions are the sacrificial animals; steadfastness is the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), and contentment likewise; the organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) are the sacrificial vessels; the organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>) are the oblations. The head is the skull-cup (<s>kapāla</s>); the hair is the sacred grass (<s>darbha</s>); the mouth is the inner altar (<s>antarvedi</s>). The head has four parts (<s>catuṣkapāla</s>); there are sixteen rows of side-teeth; one hundred and seven vital points (<s>marman</s>); one hundred and eighty joints; one hundred and nine sinews; seven hundred veins (<s>sirā</s>); five hundred portions of marrow; and indeed three hundred and sixty bones; four and a half <s>koṭi</s> (crores, i.e. forty-five million) body hairs; the heart weighs eight <s>palas</s>; the tongue twelve <s>palas</s>; one <s>prastha</s> of bile; one <s>āḍhaka</s> of phlegm; one <s>kuḍava</s> of semen; two <s>prasthas</s> of fat; urine and feces are variable, depending on the quantity of food consumed. This is the <s>Paippalāda</s> doctrine of liberation (<s>mokṣaśāstra</s>). This is the <s>Paippalāda</s> doctrine of liberation.
